mainTopic: Is the animal killed with קלון alone or תקלה alone? Includes רב המנונא's question and failed proofs from minors, and the opening of the משנה about the מגדף.
overview: The משנה gave two reasons for killing an animal used in a sin: תקלה (a person was executed because of it) and קלון (shame, since people will point at it). The גמרא asks whether both are needed. It tries to prove that תקלה alone is enough, in the case of a גוי, but this is pushed off: the משנה could instead mean that קלון alone is enough, as with a ישראל who sinned בשוגג. That is exactly רב המנונא's question. רב יוסף brings a proof from a girl aged three years and one day, and רבא brings one from a boy aged nine years and one day. Both proofs are rejected, because a minor who acts on purpose does cause real תקלה; the תורה only spares the minor, not the animal. A last attempt from the wording of the משנה also fails, because it can be read either way. So neither רב המנונא's question nor the question asked of רב ששת is settled. The amud ends by opening a new משנה: a מגדף is liable only if he says the actual Name of ה'.

steps.title: Proof from the two clauses of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The סיפא of the משנה mentions both תקלה and קלון. So the רישא must be talking about תקלה without קלון, which fits a גוי who sins with a בהמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The latter clause speaks of calamity and shame together, so the first clause must mean calamity without shame. What case is that? A gentile who has relations with an animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is trying to prove, from the wording of the משנה, that the בהמה is killed even when a גוי sinned with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives two reasons for killing the animal. The סיפא combines תקלה (a person was executed because of it) and קלון (people will point at the animal and remember the shame). If the סיפא needs both, the רישא must be a case of תקלה alone. That fits a גוי: he is executed, but his shame is not the Jewish court's concern.

keyTerms.meaning: A calamity or stumbling: here, a person was put to death because of the animal
Shame: the animal walking around reminds people of the sin
The first clause
The latter clause
And what is the case?

phrases.english: From the fact that the latter clause says calamity and shame,
the first clause must mean calamity without shame.
phrases.notes: Here 'calamity' means the person was executed because of the animal.

phrases.english: And what is the case?
A gentile who has relations with an animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier attempt to show that the animal used by a גוי is killed
steps.raayaObject: That a בהמה used by a גוי is killed even without קלון
steps.raayaSupportSource: The structure of the משנה: the סיפא lists תקלה and קלון, so the רישא must be תקלה alone

steps.title: The first clause may mean shame without calamity
steps.stepSummary: No: the רישא may be teaching that even קלון without תקלה is enough to kill the animal. That would be a ישראל who sinned בשוגג, which is the case רב המנונא asked about.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. The latter clause is calamity and shame, and the first clause teaches that even shame without calamity is enough to require killing the animal. What is the case? A Jew who sinned with an animal unintentionally, like the question of רב המנונא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof by reading the רישא the other way around.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof assumed the רישא must be 'תקלה without קלון'. The גמרא answers that it could be 'קלון without תקלה' instead. A ישראל who sinned בשוגג is not executed, so there is no תקלה, but there is still קלון. So the משנה does not have to be about a גוי at all.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it teaches us
Unintentionally
They are obligated (to kill the animal)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two readings. The proof said the רישא is תקלה with no קלון (a גוי). The rejection says the רישא is קלון with no תקלה (a ישראל בשוגג). They are opposites.

phrases.english: No. The latter clause is calamity and shame.
The first clause teaches us this:
that even shame without calamity
also obligates them to kill the animal.
And what is the case?
A Jew who has relations with an animal unintentionally,
just like the question of Rav Hamnuna.

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the inference that the רישא must be about a גוי
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The רישא can just as well mean קלון without תקלה, as with a ישראל בשוגג

steps.title: רב המנונא's question about an unintentional sinner
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא asks: if a ישראל sinned with a בהמה בשוגג, is the animal killed? Do we need both תקלה and קלון, or is קלון alone enough?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב המנונא asked: a Jew who unintentionally has relations with an animal, what is the law? Do we need calamity and shame, and here there is shame but no calamity? Or perhaps shame alone is enough, even without calamity?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes in full the question of רב המנונא that it just mentioned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether the animal is killed only when both reasons are present. In the שוגג case the person is not executed (no תקלה), but the animal still reminds people of the sin (קלון). If both are needed, the animal lives. If קלון is enough, it is killed.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked a question (raised a doubt)
What is the law?
We require
Or perhaps

steps.whyThisMatters: This question is the center of the next part of the sugya. Proofs will now be brought to answer it.

phrases.english: As Rav Hamnuna asked:

phrases.aramaic: יִשְׂרָאֵל הַבָּא עַל הַבְּהֵמָה בְּשׁוֹגֵג, מַהוּ?
phrases.english: A Jew who unintentionally has relations with an animal, what is the law?
Do we need calamity and shame,
and here there is shame but no calamity?

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִילְמָא קָלוֹן, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין תַּקָּלָה?
phrases.english: Or perhaps shame is enough, even though there is no calamity?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the question that step 2 referred to
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether קלון alone, without תקלה, is enough to require killing the animal

steps.title: רב יוסף brings a source about a three-year-old girl
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף starts to answer רב המנונא with a משנה: a girl aged three years and one day can be betrothed through relations. A יבם who has relations with her acquires her, and others are liable for אשת איש with her.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Come and hear. A girl three years and one day old is betrothed through relations. If a יבם has relations with her, he acquires her. And one is liable for her because of the prohibition of a married woman.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף is setting up a proof to answer רב המנונא's question. Here he only quotes the source; the point he takes from it comes in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source shows that relations with a girl of three years and one day count as real relations in הלכה. They work for קידושין and יבום, and they make others liable for אשת איש. רב יוסף will use this משנה to say something about the animal case.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (introduces a proof)
She is betrothed through relations
The brother-in-law who marries his brother's childless widow
He acquired her as a wife
A married woman

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: Come and hear,
a girl three years and one day old
is betrothed through relations,
and if a yavam has relations with her, he acquires her,
and one is liable for her because of the prohibition of a married woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins an attempted answer to רב המנונא's question
steps.raayaObject: The answer to רב המנונא's question about קלון without תקלה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about a girl three years and one day old (נדה 44b)

steps.title: The quoted משנה continues: more laws about the young girl
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף keeps quoting the משנה. A girl aged three years and one day is treated like an adult woman for relations: she passes on נדה impurity, eats תרומה if married to a כהן, becomes disqualified from כהונה through a disqualified man, and forbidden partners are executed because of her while she is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: And she makes the man who has relations with her impure, so that the bedding under him becomes impure like the cover above him. If she married a כהן, she may eat תרומה. If a man who is disqualified had relations with her, he made her unfit to marry into כהונה. And if any of the forbidden partners listed in the תורה had relations with her, they are executed because of her, and she is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף is still quoting the משנה he started in step 4. This step sets up the next move: the last line, 'they are executed because of her, and she is exempt,' is the line he will use as his proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every line here shows that relations with this young girl count fully, just like with an adult. The key line is the last one. The man is executed, but the girl herself is exempt because she is a minor. The גמרא will use that difference in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: the man who has relations with her
the bedding a person lies on, which can become impure
the holy portion of produce that only כהנים and their households may eat
men disqualified from כהונה (for example a חלל or ממזר)
the forbidden relations listed in the תורה
they are put to death because of her

phrases.english: And she makes the man who has relations with her impure,
phrases.notes: This is when she is a נדה. Even at this young age, she passes her impurity on to him.

phrases.english: so that he makes the bedding beneath him impure like the cover above.
If she married a כהן, she eats תרומה.
If one of the disqualified men had relations with her,
he disqualified her from the כהונה.
phrases.notes: He means she can no longer marry a כהן.

phrases.english: And if there had relations with her
one of all the forbidden partners stated in the תורה,
they are executed because of her,
and she is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the quotation of the משנה that רב יוסף began in step 4.
steps.raayaObject: Whether קלון without תקלה is enough to kill the בהמה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about a girl aged three years and one day: 'they are executed because of her, and she is exempt'

steps.title: The animal is killed even though the girl is not punished
steps.stepSummary: The phrase 'one of all the forbidden relations' includes even a בהמה. Since the girl is exempt, there is קלון but no תקלה, and yet the משנה says the animal is killed.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'One of all the forbidden relations' includes even an animal. Here there is shame but no calamity, and still the משנה teaches that they are put to death because of her.
steps.whatsHappening: Here the proof is actually made. The animal is included in 'all the forbidden relations,' and it is killed even though the girl is not punished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The girl is a minor, so she gets no punishment, and that means there is no תקלה. There is still קלון, because the animal reminds people of what happened. Since the animal is killed anyway, קלון alone seems to be enough. That would answer רב המנונא's question about a ישראל who sinned בשוגג.

keyTerms.meaning: shame, meaning the animal keeps reminding people of the sin
calamity, meaning the animal brought a person to a sin that gets punished
there is / there is not
and it teaches (the משנה says)

steps.whyThisMatters: If this proof holds, it settles רב המנונא's question: an animal is killed even when only קלון is present.

phrases.english: 'One of all the forbidden relations'
includes even an animal.
phrases.notes: So the case would be this young girl with an animal.

phrases.english: And here there is shame,
there is no calamity,
and yet it teaches: they are executed because of her.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא הָכָא דְּקָלוֹן אִיכָּא, תַּקָּלָה לֵיכָּא, וְקָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the inference from the last line of the משנה quoted in step 5.
steps.raayaObject: קלון alone, without תקלה, is enough to kill the בהמה
steps.raayaSupportSource: 'מומתין על ידה והיא פטורה' read as including a בהמה

steps.title: She acted on purpose, so there is a calamity after all
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. The girl sinned on purpose, so there is real תקלה. The תורה only spared her out of pity, and that pity does not extend to the animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since she did it on purpose, there is also a calamity. It is just that the תורה had pity on her. It had pity on her, but not on the animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down רב יוסף's proof. It says this case actually has תקלה too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A sin done on purpose is a real תקלה, even if the sinner is not punished. Her exemption is only a special mercy because she is young. That mercy covers her alone and not the animal. So this case has both תקלה and קלון, and it proves nothing about קלון alone. רב המנונא's question stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: she acted on purpose
'the Merciful One,' meaning the תורה
had pity, spared

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think 'she is exempt' means 'she did nothing wrong.' The גמרא says she really did sin on purpose. The תורה just chose not to punish her.
steps.whatToRemember: The proof from the girl aged three years and one day fails. Her case has real תקלה, because she sinned on purpose and was only spared out of pity. So we still don't know whether קלון alone is enough to kill the animal.

phrases.english: Since she is acting on purpose,
there is also a calamity,
and it is the Merciful One who had pity on her.
On her own self He had pity;
on the animal He did not have pity.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דִּמְזִידָה הִיא, תַּקָּלָה נָמֵי אִיכָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof made in step 6 by showing that its case really has תקלה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only this proof. רב המנונא's question itself remains open.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed there was no תקלה because she was exempt. But she sinned on purpose, so there is תקלה, and her exemption is only the תורה's pity for her personally.

steps.title: רבא quotes the case of a nine-year-old boy
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings a new proof from the משנה about a boy aged nine years and one day. His relations count as full relations: he acquires his יבמה, and he becomes impure like a נדה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Come and hear. A boy aged nine years and one day who has relations with his יבמה acquires her as his wife. But he cannot give her a גט until he grows up. He also becomes impure like a נדה, and makes the bedding beneath him impure like the top layer.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא starts a second attempt to answer רב המנונא by quoting the next משנה in נדה. This step only sets up the case; the proof itself comes in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, the proof came from a young girl. Now רבא switches to a young boy, aged nine years and one day. The משנה shows that his relations count as real relations in many areas of הלכה, even though he is still a minor.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: the opening for bringing a proof from a source
His יבמה: his brother's widow, whose husband died without children
He acquired her: she is now his wife
Until he grows up and reaches adulthood
Bedding, or something used for lying on

phrases.english: Rava said: Come and hear,
a boy nine years and one day old
who has relations with his brother's widow has acquired her,
but he cannot give a bill of divorce until he grows up.
And he becomes impure like a menstruating woman
so that he makes the bedding beneath him impure like the top layer.
phrases.notes: This happens when he had relations with a נדה. Her impurity passes on to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב יוסף's proof from the girl was rejected in step 7, רבא tries a new proof from the next משנה in נדה.
steps.raayaObject: רב המנונא's question: is קלון alone, without תקלה, enough to kill the animal?
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in נדה about a boy aged nine years and one day.

steps.title: The animal is stoned because of the boy
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues. The boy disqualifies a woman from תרומה but cannot make her able to eat it. He disqualifies an animal from the מזבח, and the animal is stoned because of him. Forbidden partners are executed because of him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He disqualifies her from eating תרומה, but he cannot make her able to eat it. He disqualifies an animal from being brought on the מזבח, and the animal is stoned because of him. And if he had relations with any of the forbidden relations written in the תורה, they are executed because of him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא keeps quoting the משנה and reaches the key line: an animal is stoned because of this boy. This is the line he will build his proof on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the girl case (step 6), the גמרא had to read 'one of all the forbidden relations' as including an animal. Here the משנה says it outright: the animal is stoned because of him. Still, the boy himself is a minor and is not punished.

keyTerms.meaning: Disqualifies: here, from eating תרומה or from being brought on the מזבח
Lets someone eat: makes a wife able to eat תרומה
She (the animal) is stoned
Because of him, through his act
Forbidden relations listed in the תורה

phrases.english: He disqualifies but does not enable her to eat,
phrases.notes: This is about תרומה. A disqualified boy takes it away from a כהן's daughter, but a boy who is a כהן can't give it to his wife.

phrases.english: and he disqualifies the animal
from being brought on the altar,
and it is stoned because of him.
And if he had relations with one
of all the forbidden relations stated in the Torah,
they are executed because of him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This continues the quote of the משנה that began in step 8.
steps.raayaObject: Whether קלון alone is enough to kill the animal.

steps.title: Shame without harm, yet the animal is stoned
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws the proof. Since the boy is a minor and is not punished, there is קלון but no תקלה. Yet the משנה says the animal is stoned, so קלון alone should be enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here there is קלון (shame) but no תקלה (no one is punished because of the animal). And still the משנה teaches that the animal is stoned because of him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out what רבא wants to prove from the משנה. A minor's act brings shame but no real sin, and still the animal is killed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that a minor is exempt from punishment, so nobody is executed because of this animal, and there seems to be no תקלה. If the animal is still stoned, then קלון alone must be enough. That would answer רב המנונא's question about a ישראל who sinned בשוגג.

keyTerms.meaning: Shame: the animal would remind people of the disgraceful act
A stumbling: the animal caused a person to commit a real sin
It teaches: the source says this

phrases.english: But here there is shame,
but there is no calamity,
and yet it teaches: it is stoned because of him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This draws the conclusion from the משנה line quoted in step 9.
steps.raayaObject: קלון alone, without תקלה, is enough to kill the animal.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The boy is exempt, yet the animal is stoned because of him.

steps.title: The boy acted on purpose, so there is real harm
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. The boy did the act on purpose, so there is real תקלה. The תורה only spared him out of pity, and that pity does not cover the animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since he did it on purpose, there is תקלה too. It is only that the Merciful One had pity on him. The Merciful One had pity on him, but did not have pity on the animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away רבא's proof using the same reasoning it used for the girl in step 7.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A nine-year-old who knowingly does the act really did something wrong, so the animal did cause a real תקלה. He is free from punishment only because the תורה pities a minor, not because no sin happened. So the case still has both קלון and תקלה, and it says nothing about a case of קלון alone.

keyTerms.meaning: On purpose, knowingly
The Merciful One: a name for ה׳, as the Giver of the תורה
Had pity, spared

steps.whatToRemember: Both proofs, from the girl and from the boy, fail for the same reason. A minor who acts on purpose still causes real תקלה. The תורה only spares the minor himself, not the animal. So רב המנונא's question is still open.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think 'exempt from punishment' means 'no sin happened.' The גמרא says the minor's act is a real sin. He just isn't punished, out of the תורה's pity.

phrases.english: Since he acted on purpose,
there is a calamity as well,
and it is the Merciful One who had pity on him.
On him himself the Merciful One had pity,
on the animal the Merciful One did not have pity.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דְּמֵזִיד הוּא, תַּקָּלָה נָמֵי אִיכָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This rejects the proof drawn in step 10.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבא's whole proof from the nine-year-old boy.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed there was no תקלה. But a minor who acts on purpose does cause real תקלה; he is only spared from punishment out of pity.

steps.title: A new proof from the second reason in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the second reason the משנה gives for stoning the animal: so people won't point at it in the market and remember the sinner.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: another reason is so that the animal will not walk through the market and people will say, 'This is the one that caused so-and-so to be stoned.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new attempt to answer the question by quoting a line from the משנה. This step only sets up the proof. The actual argument comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gave two reasons for killing the animal. The first is that a sin came to a person through it (תקלה). The second, quoted here, is the shame it brings (קלון). The גמרא will now read these two reasons against each other.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: the opening for a proof from a source
Another explanation, or a second reason
So-and-so, an unnamed person
Marketplace

phrases.english: Come and hear:
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה from earlier, on 54a, about why the animal is stoned.

phrases.english: Alternatively,
so that the animal will not pass through the marketplace
and people will say: "This is the one
because of which so-and-so was stoned."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof from the nine-year-old boy was rejected, the גמרא brings a new source.
steps.raayaObject: Whether קלון without תקלה is enough to require stoning the animal
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה on 54a, second reason (דבר אחר)

steps.title: Inferring that the first reason means shame without sin
steps.stepSummary: Since the second reason includes both תקלה and קלון, the first reason must be about קלון alone. An example is a Jew who sinned with an animal by accident.
steps.simpleTranslation: Doesn't this show that, since the second reason is a case of both calamity and shame, the first reason is a case of shame without calamity? What case is that? A Jew who had relations with an animal by accident.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the proof. It reads the first reason in the משנה as a case where there is shame but no real sin, and the animal is still stoned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the second reason covers a case with both elements, the first must cover a case with only one. The גמרא says that one is קלון. A Jew who sinned by accident is not executed, so there is no תקלה. But it is still shameful, and the animal is stoned. That would prove קלון alone is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't it that...? It introduces a suggested inference
The latter part of a source
The first part of a source
What is the case? How do we picture it?
By accident, without intent

phrases.english: What, is it not
that since the latter part is calamity and shame,
phrases.notes: The latter part is the market reason just quoted in the previous step.

phrases.english: the first part is shame without calamity?
And what is the case?
A Jew who has relations with an animal unintentionally.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the inference from the משנה quoted in step 12.
steps.raayaObject: קלון without תקלה is enough for the animal to be stoned
steps.raayaSupportSource: Contrasting the רישא and סיפא of the משנה, with the case of a Jew who sinned בשוגג

steps.title: Rejected: the first reason may mean sin without shame
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. The first reason could instead be תקלה without קלון, as with a גוי. That is the same question asked of רב ששת, which was never answered.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. The second reason is calamity and shame, but the first could be calamity without shame. What case is that? A non-Jew who had relations with an animal, which is exactly what they asked רב ששת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the proof. It reads the first reason the other way around, so the משנה proves nothing about our question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא simply flips the reading back: the first reason could be תקלה without קלון. A גוי who does this is executed, so there is תקלה. But his shame is not the Jewish court's concern, so there is no קלון. Whether such an animal is stoned is the open question put to רב ששת, so we cannot learn anything from it. Both questions stay unresolved.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-Jew
אמורא who was asked whether the animal is stoned when a גוי sins with it
As they asked of him: a reference to an earlier open question

steps.whatToRemember: No source settles it. We still don't know whether קלון alone or תקלה alone is enough to stone the animal. The question stays open, together with the question asked of רב ששת.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא proved that תקלה without קלון is enough. It only showed the משנה could be read that way, so it can't serve as a proof either way.

phrases.english: No,
the latter part is calamity and shame,
the first part is calamity without shame.
And what is the case?
A gentile who has relations with an animal,
just as they asked of רב ששת.
phrases.notes: This points back to the earlier question asked of רב ששת. It was never answered, so this case can't prove anything.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, סֵיפָא תַּקָּלָה וְקָלוֹן, רֵישָׁא תַּקָּלָה בְּלֹא קָלוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference of step 13 by reading the רישא the opposite way.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Fully cancels the proof from the משנה. The question remains unresolved.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The רישא can be read as תקלה without קלון (a גוי), not קלון without תקלה. The status of that case is itself the unanswered question asked of רב ששת.

steps.title: New משנה: the blasphemer is liable only for saying the Name
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה opens. A מגדף is not liable unless he says the actual Name of ה'. רבי יהושע בן קרחה begins to add a teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A person who curses ה' is not liable unless he clearly says the Name. רבי יהושע בן קרחה said:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a brand-new משנה about the מגדף, one of those who are stoned. The last words begin a teaching from רבי יהושע בן קרחה that continues past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה limits the death penalty: cursing ה' in general terms, without saying His actual Name, does not make one liable. רבי יהושע בן קרחה is about to explain how the case is handled in court.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
One who curses ה' (a blasphemer)
That he clearly says the actual Name of ה'
תנא who adds a teaching about the מגדף

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who blasphemes is not liable
unless he utters the Name.
phrases.notes: Literally, until he spells out the Name. He has to say the actual Name of ה', not just a general curse.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha said:

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הַמְגַדֵּף אֵינוֹ חַיָּיב עַד שֶׁיְּפָרֵשׁ הַשֵּׁם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the animal discussion and opens a new topic: the מגדף.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מגדף is liable only if he pronounces the actual Name of ה'.
